---
title: "Sample Replicates"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = FALSE
)
```

EnMoDS data includes some replicate samples, usually defined as quality control (QC) samples alongside regular
environmental samples. The `QC_Type` column identifies which kind of sample each
row comes from. 

Other samples may have replicates due to multiple analysis methods, such as Phosphorus Total, or field vs. lab pH.

## QC types

According to the [QC_Types.xlsx from EnMoDS](https://coms.api.gov.bc.ca/api/v1/object/52b1636f-3cd6-4f8c-b49e-a81f12f6bd18), the types are "Blank", "Other QC", "Regular", "Replicate", or "Spike".

However in the data itself, they appear to be "BLANK", "NORMAL", "REPLICATE" and "SPIKE".

**Current practice is to only keep NORMAL samples when applying formatting functions**.

### Example

```{r}
library(bcgwcat2)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

# A well sampled on one day, with normal, replicate and blank samples
s <- fetch_renmods("E316790", c("2023-10-11", "2023-10-12"))
nrow(s)
count(s, QC_Type)

s <- fmt_minimal(s)
nrow(s) # drops unused observedproperties, as well as non-normal samples
```


## Multiple Analyses

```{r}
s <- fetch_renmods("E337477", c("2025-06-17", "2025-06-18"))
fmt_minimal(s)

filter(s, Observed_Property_ID == "Phosphorus Total Dissolved")


s |>
  filter(str_detect(Observed_Property_ID, "pH")) |>
  select(
    Location_ID,
    Observed_Date_Time,
    Observed_Property_ID,
    Data_Classification,
    Analysis_Method,
    QC_Type,
    Result_Value
  )

fmt <- fmt_minimal(s)
fmt |>
  filter(str_detect(observed_property_id, "pH")) |>
  select(
    location_id,
    observed_date_time,
    observed_property_id,
    analysis_method,
    result_value
  )
```

## Multiple pH Measures

In the EMS data, `pH`, EMS ID 004, was considered as the Lab whereas `pH-Field`, EMS ID PH-F was a field based pH value. 

In EnMoDs this is a bit confused. There is `pH (acidity)` which is associated with EMS code: 0004 and `pH-Field (acidity)` associated with EMS code `PH-F`. 

However, EnMoDs also includes a `Data_Classification` column which can be "LAB", "FIELD_RESULT", "ACTIVITY_RESULT", "SURROGATE_RESULT", "FIELD_SURVEY", and "VERTICAL_PROFILE" (according to [Data_Classifications.xlsx from the EnMoDs website](https://coms.api.gov.bc.ca/api/v1/object/18a23c82-4fef-472d-8f9a-263fd7bc1870)). 

This leads to observations having two measures of `pH (acidity)`, on of which has a `Data_Classification` of "LAB" and the other of "FIELD_RESULT".

**Current practice is to relabel those with a `Data_Classification` of "FIELD_RESULT" as `pH-Field (acidity)`. If this duplicates an existing `pH-Field (acidity)` record, it is removed.**.

```{r}
s <- fetch_renmods("E337477", c("2025-06-17", "2025-06-18"))

s |>
  filter(str_detect(Observed_Property_ID, "pH")) |>
  select(
    Location_ID,
    Observed_Date_Time,
    Observed_Property_ID,
    Data_Classification,
    Analysis_Method,
    QC_Type,
    Result_Value
  )

fmt <- fmt_minimal(s)
fmt |>
  filter(str_detect(observed_property_id, "pH")) |>
  select(
    location_id,
    observed_date_time,
    observed_property_id,
    analysis_method,
    result_value
  )
```

Very rarely this actually creates a duplicate of the existing `pH-Field` value.


```{r}
s <- fetch_renmods("E287195", c("2022-02-23", "2022-02-24"))

s |>
  filter(str_detect(Observed_Property_ID, "pH")) |>
  select(
    Location_ID,
    Observed_Date_Time,
    Observed_Property_ID,
    Data_Classification,
    Analysis_Method,
    QC_Type,
    Result_Value
  ) |>
  arrange(Observed_Property_ID)

fmt <- fmt_minimal(s)
fmt |>
  filter(str_detect(observed_property_id, "pH")) |>
  select(
    location_id,
    observed_date_time,
    observed_property_id,
    analysis_method,
    result_value
  ) |>
  arrange(observed_property_id)
```
